brief: `cloudCover()` veils the sun's disc, but nothing on the ground was ever told. Every cast shadow in the town — walls and eaves, trees, people, the tile-level shadows — is thrown at a fixed alpha off `SUN[0]/SUN[2]`, so under 0.95 cover the sky is a grey lid and the lane beneath it is still full of crisp midday shadows. Under real overcast a shadow does not merely fade, it spreads, because the source stops being a point. Fade and soften the shadow sites together off ONE term read by all of them, neutral at low cover so a fair day is byte-identical. Why now: b20 turns heavy overcast from a rare event into most of a winter, so this goes from a cosmetic nit to a defect on screen for a large share of the year.
successLooksLike: Pinned at one instant with cover forced to 0.1 and then to 0.95, the wide shot goes from hard-edged shadows to none worth the name, gradually rather than as a switch, and nothing else in the frame moves.
avoid: Do not touch `sunVec` or the lit-side shading on roofs and ground — that is already veiled through the sky colours, and moving both is how you end up with a flat grey world instead of an overcast one. This brief is only the CAST shadows. One definition read by every site, not six separate tunings: there are roughly six call sites and they will drift apart within two iterations if you tune them individually.
